drift_summary.delta_shape: pydantic 2.13.4 emits `Literal['refused']` as `const: refused` WITHOUT the redundant `enum: ['refused']`. Prior pydantic (2.x <=~2.10) emitted BOTH.

drift_introduced_at.wave: NONE (environmental — no wave modified this model)

intended_vs_unintended_judgement.reasoning: No wave scope modified AdmissionRefusal_v0. The drift is a pydantic-emitter behavior change; the model code is unchanged since the snapshot was frozen. This is NOT an intended model edit and NOT the FL-P4-W4-01 defect class (which is 'code changed, snapshot forgotten'). It IS a hitherto-unnamed defect class: 'library upgrade silently drifted snapshot semantics'.

reconciliation.rationale: The alternative — pinning pydantic to a version that emits the old shape, or rewriting the invariant to project schemas onto a version-independent canonical form — is out of W6 scope (touches every frozen contract test). The snapshot is the anchor of a behavior contract, and the runtime behavior of AdmissionRefusal_v0 is UNCHANGED. Owner ruling of W6 close reconciliation IS the ratification moment. The alternative is named as an explicit follow-up (see process_finding).
reconciliation.alternative_rejected_because: there is no code change to revert — the drift is in pydantic's schema emitter, not in AdmissionRefusal_v0 itself.

process_finding: Frozen snapshots stored as raw pydantic-emitted JSON are NOT stable across pydantic minor versions. A P1 backlog item is opened (see notes/w6_close_report.md §Process-Findings) to either (a) pin pydantic in requirements.txt with justification, or (b) project schemas through a version-independent canonical form (strip pydantic-idiomatic redundancy such as the 'enum' companion to 'const') before byte-comparison. Not remediated in W6 — flagged for owner ruling in W7 opener.
